evidence: PlaceOrderUseCase.toResponse, UpdateOrderStateUseCase.execute and ListOrdersByStateUseCase.execute each map id/customerId/getState()/items/createdAt.toISOString() by hand
DTOs.ts: CreateOrderResponse and UpdateOrderStateResponse have identical fields; ListOrdersResponse.orders declares the same shape again inline
DTOs.ts declares CancelOrderRequest, which nothing uses; UpdateOrderStateUseCase.execute(orderId, newState) ignores UpdateOrderStateRequest
ListOrdersByStateUseCase constructor injects productRepository but never uses it
GetProductStockUseCase.execute and executeAll build the same {productId, name, stock} object twice
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one cohesive concern (order and product use cases), but rules are copied across files instead of kept in one place. (1) Three use cases each build the order response by hand. (2) DTOs.ts declares the same order response shape three times. (3) CancelOrderUseCase decides which states can be cancelled outside the domain's transitionTo method; Order.ts wasn't provided, so whether transitionTo also enforces this is unconfirmed. (4) The module's own DTOs are used unevenly: CancelOrderRequest is unused, UpdateOrderStateRequest is bypassed, and ListOrdersByStateUseCase injects a repository it never uses. (5) GetProductStockUseCase builds the stock response twice.

violations.message: execute() copies the Order-to-response mapping that also appears in PlaceOrderUseCase.toResponse and ListOrdersByStateUseCase; it also takes raw arguments instead of the UpdateOrderStateRequest DTO.
execute() copies the Order-to-response mapping inline, and the constructor injects a productRepository that is never used.
private toResponse() is one of three separate copies of the Order-to-response mapping in the module; it should be shared.
CreateOrderResponse, UpdateOrderStateResponse and ListOrdersResponse.orders each declare the same order shape; CancelOrderRequest is declared but never used.
Hard-codes the shipped/delivered cancellation rule outside Order.transitionTo, so the state-transition rule lives in two places.
execute() and executeAll() each build the same ProductStockResponse object instead of sharing one mapper.
